verdict.rationale: Elicit's first-party export docs cover all three parts of the story. Research Reports export as PDF or Word on every plan, tables export as CSV and Excel, and the Library and certain source tables export as RIS or BIB for Zotero, Mendeley and EndNote. The pricing page also lists export to RIS, CSV, BIB, PDF and DOCX. Systematic Review table export is limited to Pro, Scale and Enterprise plans. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the export features, and spreadsheet export for Systematic Review tables on free or lower plans.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can export results to common formats, including documents, spreadsheets, and reference-manager files

citations.quote: Research Reports can be exported as a PDF or Word file, regardless of which Elicit plan you subscribe to.
Tables can be exported in CSV and Excel format. Certain tables of sources can be exported as RIS or BIB files.
Your Elicit Library can be exported as a .ris file, which you can import into Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote, or another reference manager.
Export to RIS, CSV, BIB, PDF and DOCX
